historical_reviews.v3_1: Warm reboot stability must prove the entire reset-to-readiness transition while auxiliary power remains present. A cycle is complete only after console/OS services and PCIe enumeration reach defined readiness, full lspci is normalized against baseline, and newly appended SEL/OS events are assessed; otherwise a fast partial boot can be counted as success.

original_test_intent: Stress repeated warm OS reboot recovery and verify the SUT never hangs, PCIe inventory remains stable, the system remains usable and no stress-related BMC or OS errors appear.
original_method: On a dedicated drained SUT, define an exact count for the 1500-minute plan, capture immutable baseline and cycle-ID pre-state, request one approved warm reboot through the chosen OS/BMC path, monitor console/BMC/OS readiness to a bounded timeout, collect complete post-boot lspci and new SEL/OS events, normalize/compare and continue only after every gate passes.
manual_activity: The platform owner approves the dedicated SUT, exact warm-reboot count, trigger/readiness/error criteria and independent recovery before the stress run.
required_inputs: Per-cycle boot and service readiness timeout
BMC SEL and OS event severity/time window criteria
safety_requirements: Never reboot an active production target
Use a bounded owner-approved cycle count
Preserve all pre-existing and new logs
Verify exact target before each reboot
Stop on first hang, timeout, inventory drift or relevant error
Do not issue another reboot before full readiness review
Do not auto-retry a failed cycle
Do not change boot or PCIe configuration
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, workload drain, tools and recovery
Collect baseline and immutable cycle pre-state
Trigger exactly one approved warm reboot
Monitor BMC/console/OS phase timing and readiness
Collect complete lspci and incremental SEL/OS event evidence
Validate final health and archive results without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve count, trigger and readiness criteria
Resolve PCIe inventory or boot-duration variance
Stop and lead recovery after any failure

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The pre-reboot inventory commands are relevant but use unsafe SSH and overwrite fixed `/tmp` files. They do not implement the source's post-reboot recovery, complete per-cycle lspci comparison, SEL/OS error inspection or hang timeout.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a cycle-ID orchestrator with verified access to capture immutable full lspci plus log cursors, request one approved warm reboot, monitor phased readiness, collect post-state and incremental SEL/OS events, compare, and stop before any next cycle on anomaly.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The warm-reset mechanism, long-term objective, 1500-minute machine duration and lspci-focused acceptance remain; owner supplies the exact bounded cycle count.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: For every cycle, preserve pre-state and log cursors, measure reboot/firmware/kernel/service readiness, then compare complete PCIe inventory and only the new SEL/OS event interval before advancing.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds bounded count, cycle identity, post-boot readiness, incremental error assessment and no-retry recovery while preserving warm-reboot semantics.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Files written before reboot and overwritten next cycle cannot prove any recovery; reachability alone can return before PCIe drivers and services are stable.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Repeated reboots interrupt all host workloads and can expose boot loops or management loss; log noise must be classified against approved severity/time criteria rather than requiring literal emptiness.

project_override_considerations: Approve the exact warm reboot command/path, cycle count within 1500 minutes, firmware/OS/service readiness milestones, allowable PCIe ordering changes, relevant SEL/OS error definitions and owner-led boot-loop recovery.
expected_evidence: SUT/BMC/BIOS/OS identity, dedicated/workload state, approved count/trigger/timeouts
Baseline lspci and log cursors, tool versions and synchronized timestamps
Immutable per-cycle reboot request, console/BMC/OS readiness timeline and exit status
Complete pre/post normalized lspci comparison and newly appended SEL/OS event assessment
First-failure/no-retry audit, final workable-state proof, preserved logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently describe long-term warm reboot with lspci stability and error-free recovery. `Long term` lacks a count but does not conflict with the 1500-minute duration.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The warm-reboot purpose and acceptance are clear. Count, trigger, readiness and recovery are identifiable execution prerequisites, so classification is REQUIRES.

review_improvement: Replaces overwritten pre-reboot snapshots with an immutable cycle ledger that proves complete warm-boot recovery, PCIe stability and source-required error absence before every next reboot.
independent_technical_reasoning: Warm reset retains standby power and may preserve BMC or device state that a cold cycle clears, so its failures often present as accumulated initialization or driver issues. Capturing only the next lspci output cannot show when or how readiness failed. A per-cycle timeline and incremental log window distinguish a hang, slow enumeration and a genuine PCIe inventory change while preventing additional reboots from erasing the failure context.
